title: CHK-7's adversary is strictly weaker than the model's real input set: profiles + channels every arm already receives form a near-complete symbolic answer key that CHK-7 cannot see
detail: The frozen P1.3 architecture the spec reuses (C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_dev_gpu_pilot_v1/run_pilot_v3.py) feeds EVERY arm three channels beyond profiles: (1) m_loc, the candidate-by-clause occurrence matrix (extract_clause_local); (2) discourse positions (the profile sequence is indexed by clause order); (3) g, an embedding of the FULL question text (spans.py build_input_text appends the whole question, including named anchors X and M and the class-naming wording like 'drawn to'). Given (profile sequence, m_loc, positions, question anchors, question type), every v0.1 family is symbolically solvable WITHOUT reading clause semantics: QB-REL = find the ^3-profile clause containing anchor X, take its co-member mind (entity type is inferable because minds/ideas/parts are disjoint vocabularies with distinct membership patterns), then the ^2-profile clause co-membered with that mind, then its object. QB-ORD adds 'position > pivot' read straight off the profile sequence. QB-COMP chains membership. QB-INT is repeated-part membership. Residual ambiguity is only intra-clause role assignment in ^8 (source vs surfaced idea). So clause-membership + order + anchors reconstruct the operation graph's EDGES, and the profile supplies the missing class LABELS — the profile completes an answer key jointly with channels every arm receives. CHK-7's B-KEY (profiles + question TYPE + candidate list, 'NO text, NO graph', PATH_B_TASK_SPEC_v0_1.md line 102) never sees membership, anchors, or question wording, so it certifies nothing about this composite key. Consequences: Q-B2 (S3 vs S-PERM/S-ALT) stays fair (all class-distinguishing arms complete the same key), but Q-B1's licensed reading 'typing helps multi-hop relational READING' is wrong — typing may help by completing a symbolic shortcut that bypasses reading entirely. Fixes: (a) redefine B-KEY's input to the honest set — profiles, question type, question surface (or at minimum: which candidates are named in the question + the final-hop-class cue), the ordered candidate list, the candidate-clause membership matrix, and discourse positions; (b) add a B-MEMBER baseline (true classes + membership + positions + anchors, no clause text) next to B-TYPEONLY — if B-MEMBER ≈ 1.0, the honest statement is that PATH B moved the key from (profile, qtype) to (profile, qtype, membership, order, anchors), and profile-arm headroom must be reported against B-MEMBER, not against uniform.

title: CHK-7 as written is broken in both directions: a hand-coded B-KEY passes vacuously, while an honestly optimized B-KEY on the declared inputs likely exceeds uniform+0.05 through structural type/position priors that are not a disguised answer key
detail: The spec does not say B-KEY is TRAINED to exploit its inputs; a fixed hand-written solver will miss real channels and the ceiling passes dishonestly. Conversely, a learned B-KEY on exactly the declared inputs (profiles sequence, qtype, candidate list) can beat candidate-uniform+0.05 without any answer key: (1) qtype fixes the answer's entity TYPE (QB-INT → part, others → idea), and type is recoverable from candidate-list structure because v1 candidate order is first-mention discourse order (generate_construction_gold.py builds 'ents' by iterating shuffled ops; the spec's §2.3 'closed entity set' carries this over silently) — the profile sequence predicts per-clause new-candidate index ranges (^2/^3 introduce ≤2 entities, ^6 up to 4, ^8 up to 3), letting a trained solver segment the list by type; a type prior alone (e.g., 12 candidates, 5 ideas) gives 0.20 vs uniform 0.083, blowing past +0.05. (2) QB-INT's answer sits in the FIRST ^6 clause's part index range (deduplication gives the repeated part no second slot). (3) QB-ORD 'after'-questions favor later same-class index ranges. So the gate either fires PATHB_CONSTRUCTION_FAILED on an honest construction (type priors are inherent to any typed QA task) or is run weak and passes as paper. Fix: define B-KEY as an optimized/trained adversary (fit on train, scored on val) and gate on the PROFILE INCREMENT — acc(B-KEY with profiles) − acc(B-KEY without profiles) ≤ 0.05, per family — while reporting absolutes; and add a candidate-order law (per-passage seeded shuffle of the candidate list) to kill the index-arithmetic channel for model and adversary alike.

title: QB-INT uniqueness enforcement creates a profile-free counting shortcut: the answer is the unique part token that occurs twice — a B0 surface shortcut the spec should register, and CHK-3's edge-usage trace wrongly counts these as compositional
detail: Parts otherwise occur exactly once per passage (each ^6 lists distinct parts); the generator's guaranteed-unique intersection element is therefore the only repeated part-type token in the raw text, and the family is identifiable from question surface ('which part lay inside both...'). B0 heuristic 'return the twice-occurring part' solves QB-INT ≈100% with no graph, no profiles, no typing. Two required responses: (1) REGISTER this in the B0-SURF family (spec §6 leaves B0's contents unenumerated — the headline B1−B0 'cost of the bijection break' is manipulable by choosing a weak B0); or defeat it generator-side by requiring a second overlapping ^6 pair whose shared part does not satisfy the question's anchors, so counting yields ≥2 candidates and only the graph anchors decide. (2) CHK-3 ('≥50% of questions require ≥2 graph edges per the frozen solver's edge-usage trace', line 98) measures the ORACLE's route, not the task's minimal information requirement — a question the solver answers with 3 edges can still fall to a 0-edge counting shortcut. Composition-necessity should be evidenced by a registered shortcut-battery FAILING, not by the solver's own trace.

title: CHK-1's ≥95% threshold leaves an aggregate bijective loophole larger than the frozen ≥0.02 decision margin, and '≥2 candidate objects' is defeatable by question-anchor exclusion
detail: Up to 5% of passages (≈50 of 1,000 val) may be v1-style class-bijective. A typing arm that exploits only those gains up to ≈+0.04–0.05 mean accuracy over a non-typing arm near uniform on them — alone exceeding the interpretation law's ≥0.02 threshold (spec line 162), so a Q-B1 'typing helps' margin could be manufactured entirely inside the loophole with every check green. Three sub-holes: (a) if one of the ≥2 final-hop-class objects is an entity NAMED in the question (permitted, even encouraged, by G-overlap), the trivial heuristic 'exclude the question-named anchor' restores bijectivity — CHK-1 must count candidate objects EXCLUDING question-named entities; (b) '≥2 candidate objects' should read ≥2 DISTINCT objects (two same-class clauses may share an object); (c) B-1OP (CHK-4 ≤0.25) is only meaningful if its non-unique-clause behavior is defined as a uniform guess among final-hop-class objects — an abstaining matcher makes ≤0.25 a bound on a strawman. Fix: raise CHK-1 to 100% via generator-side exclusion (v1's registered distractor law already achieved 100% on attract/avert per CONSTRUCTION_GOLD_DATASET_SPEC.md), define the count anchor-excluded and distinct, and report per family.

title: All aggregate gate thresholds (CHK-1/CHK-4/CHK-7) can hide one fully-keyed question family; QB-ORD's 'after'-only wording plus uniqueness guarantees a family-specific discourse-position shortcut
detail: With five families, CHK-4's aggregate ≤0.25 permits ONE family to be ~100% single-op solvable (≈0.20 contribution); CHK-7's aggregate ceiling lets one fully-keyed family hide diluted by four; and candidate-uniform itself differs per family (QB-INT passages carry more parts, hence larger candidate sets and lower uniform), so an aggregate uniform reference is wrong. Separately, QB-ORD as drafted (§2.3) uses only 'after': for the answer to be unique the generator must place exactly one same-mind final-hop clause after the pivot, so 'take the LAST final-hop-class object (for that mind)' becomes a near-exact heuristic; the version using only the profile sequence and candidate order ('latest same-class index range') is even inside CHK-7's currently declared inputs. Fixes: run CHK-1, CHK-4, and CHK-7 PER FAMILY with per-family uniform references; add before/after-balanced QB-ORD templates; and audit that same-class distractor clauses fall on both sides of the pivot so direction wording alone never determines the answer.

title: S-ALT certificate contradicts the Delta.2 protocol it claims to reuse, and v1 history predicts it fails — requirement 6 coverage collapses
detail: Spec section 5 (C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_path_b_v2/PATH_B_TASK_SPEC_v0_1.md, lines 149-156) defines S-ALT as a WordNet construction under the 'S7-Delta.2 magnitude-gate protocol reused', while CHK-6 requires S-ALT to be 'a confusion-free mapping verb->class up to relabeling' — i.e., an EXACT bijection of the true typing. These are mutually exclusive: the Delta.2 admission gates (cjt_dev_gpu_pilot_v1/README.md, Delta.2 round) required the control to be '!= S3 under all 24 permutations' with D_copy = 0.476 > 0.25 — the protocol ADMITS only non-copies, CHK-6 DEMANDS a perfect copy up to relabeling. One gate forbids what the other requires; as written S-ALT cannot pass both. Separately, the v1 record makes the confusion-free certificate empirically implausible for ANY honest independent construction: on 16 verbs chosen to instantiate the 4 operations, the best honest hard partition (S7-H) reached only A* = 7/16 agreement, the soft construction A_hard* = 11/16, and the S7-P landscape (S7_PILOT_BUILD_RECEIPT.json) showed no semantic WordNet carving even reached orthogonality, let alone perfection. A new 32-verb inventory is still selected to instantiate the same 4 classes, so a 32/32 confusion-free WordNet mapping is a predictable failure. The spec's fallback ('S-ALT is dropped and the fact recorded — S-PERM alone already carries the Q-B2 comparison') then makes requirement 6 ('ordinary semantic controls receive EQUALLY USEFUL information') rest entirely on S-PERM, which is not an ordinary semantic control — it is a relabeling of the answer-generating typing itself. And if S-ALT somehow DID pass the certificate, its per-clause profiles would be exactly a fixed bijection of S3's profiles — indistinguishable at the model input from S-PERM (provenance is invisible to the model), so it would add zero scientific content. The spec must say all of this: (1) resolve the CHK-6 vs Delta.2 contradiction; (2) state that certified-S-ALT is model-equivalent to S-PERM and what, if anything, distinguishes them scientifically (answer: nothing at the input level); (3) surface to the owner that requirement 6, read as 'equal information at 4 classes', is satisfiable ONLY by relabelings — an honest alternative is to register a NON-bijective honest taxonomy with its mutual information against the true typing REPORTED, turning Q-B2 into a dose-response comparison instead of an all-or-nothing certificate.

title: S3 vs S-PERM is decided a priori by architecture symmetry — the expected 'tie' is a theorem, not a finding, and CHK-6's bijection-only rule makes every admissible control vacuous
detail: In the frozen P1.3 architecture (run_pilot_v3.py lines 188-215), profiles enter at exactly one point: the router score s_i = content + lambda*(W_r g . p_i), with W_r a learned Linear(896,4). A frozen class permutation P of the profile columns satisfies (W_r g).(P p) = (P^T W_r g).p, so the S-PERM arm's loss landscape is the S3 landscape under the reparameterization W_r -> P^T W_r. The init distribution of W_r is row-permutation-invariant and AdamW is coordinate-wise (permutation-equivariant), so S3 and S-PERM are DISTRIBUTIONALLY IDENTICAL training problems; any observed difference is seed noise. Consequences the spec does not state: (1) Q-B2's 'expected honest outcome is a TIE; a tie here is a finding, not a failure' (spec lines 33-36) oversells — the tie is architecturally guaranteed and carries no empirical information about CAS identity; (2) a stable S3 > S-PERM gap of >= 0.02 is not merely 'an anomaly to be investigated' — it is near-proof of a pipeline bug (profile-table leak, assembly error, seed mishandling), and the law should say so with that specific diagnosis; (3) because CHK-6 admits ONLY 'class-distinguishing bijection' controls (or the undefined 'matched-ensemble member'), every control it can ever certify is equivalent to S3 by the same argument — CHK-6 is self-defeating for Q-B2: it admits exactly the controls whose tie is guaranteed. The only informative equal-power control would differ in STRUCTURE while matching distinguishing power, which at 4 classes is impossible (equal power <=> same partition up to renaming). The spec should state the equivariance argument explicitly and reframe what S-PERM actually tests: implementation integrity, not scientific identity.

title: Frozen P1.3 architecture cannot represent the PATH B task: MAX_IDEAS = 6 vs K in 6..9 clauses
detail: Spec section 2.2 sets K in 6..9 clauses per passage, and section 5 freezes 'the FROZEN P1.3 architecture ... with no modification'. But the frozen pipeline hard-caps at 6 clauses: exec/arms.py line 21 declares MAX_IDEAS = 6, imported by run_pilot_v3.py (line 58) and used to size every batch tensor (pack_batches_v3 line 134: h = torch.zeros(b, MAX_IDEAS, D_MODEL)). For a 7-9-clause passage, extract_split (exec/activation_extraction.py) returns h_ideas with N=7..9 rows and the assignment h[j, :n] = f['h'] at run_pilot_v3.py line 148 raises a RuntimeError (shape mismatch), while extract_clause_local's packing guard 'if i < MAX_IDEAS' (line 156) SILENTLY DROPS clause-local candidate evidence for clauses 7-9 — so the failure mode is a mix of crash and silent truncation. If the answer's only clause-local occurrence is in a dropped clause, the answer is masked out and structurally unanswerable (the code's own sanity counter 'answers with no clause-local occurrence' would fire). The v1 adversarial review already recorded that 74.6% of v1 records have <6 clauses — the constant was tuned for the v1 task. Raising MAX_IDEAS is a one-line, capacity-neutral change, but it IS a modification of the frozen architecture and must be declared, justified, and frozen at v0.2 rather than discovered at P0. As written, the spec's 'no modification' clause and section 2.2 cannot both hold.

title: QB-ORD depends on discourse order, but no executable check verifies order information is recoverable by the frozen features, and the profile channel is provably order-blind
detail: The frozen head contains NO explicit positional feature: run_pilot_v3.py's MixtureHead treats clause index equivariantly (same linear maps per clause; no positional encoding added; batch order carries no signal the head can read as order). Discourse position is available only IMPLICITLY: h_i, e_ic, and g are layer-18 states of the causal Qwen over the full passage (exec/spans.py joins clauses in discourse order, exec/activation_extraction.py means the contextual token states), so a later clause's states have attended over earlier clauses and in principle encode relative order. So the task is not provably unanswerable — but the spec never analyzes this, and none of CHK-1..7 verifies order recoverability. Three concrete gaps: (1) no pre-GPU executable check that order can be read from the features (e.g., a frozen linear probe recovering clause index or pairwise before/after relations from cached h_i, gated before spend — analogous to the pilot-law smoke gates); (2) the profile channel is structurally USELESS for QB-ORD's final disambiguation: the two competing clauses are same-class by construction (G-order), hence have IDENTICAL profiles, so s_i's profile term cannot separate them — S3's hypothesized advantage is absent by design on this family, which the interpretation law should anticipate when reading per-family results; (3) B-TYPEONLY (spec section 6) is 'expected 1.000' given 'the TRUE per-clause classes and the graph edges but not the text' — but QB-ORD is unanswerable from classes+edges without the discourse-order component of the trace, and no baseline can answer anything without a structured form of the question (type + argument entities), which 'not the text' does not specify it receives. As written the 1.000 expectation is unachievable; the input contract for B-TYPEONLY (order included, parsed question included) must be made explicit.

title: Requirement 5 carve-out: v1 verbs allowed in question templates contradicts CHK-5's letter, or silently exempts the question surface from 'unseen verbs AND sentence forms'
detail: Spec section 3 retires the 16 v1 verbs from clause rendering but permits them 'in question templates only if frozen so', while CHK-5 requires 'zero verb overlap AND zero template-form overlap between train and val/protected surfaces'. If 'surfaces' includes question text, the carve-out violates CHK-5 as written; if it excludes question text, then question wording — which necessarily contains operation-denoting verbs ('recoiled from', 'drawn to', 'captivated' in the spec's own QB examples) — may be IDENTICAL between train and val, meaning part of the val surface is seen surface. This inherits v1's recorded stance verbatim (CONSTRUCTION_GOLD_DATASET_SPEC.md lines 52-55: 'question wording is constant across splits ... a known, recorded characteristic ... not a split leak', including the recorded 'drawn' overlap with a train-only clause family) without restating it as a scoping decision under the owner's requirement 5, which says 'unseen verbs AND sentence forms' with no question exemption. The leak is real but bounded: constant question verbs let the model carry a question-verb -> final-hop-class mapping from train into val — exactly the op-identification surface that requirement 4 aims to demote (CHK-4 bounds only the clause-side single-op matcher, not question-side type reading, which every arm legitimately needs). Resolution needed at v0.2: either (a) make question-template verb inventories and forms split-disjoint too (strong reading), or (b) explicitly scope requirement 5 to clause surfaces, define 'frozen so' precisely (which verbs, which templates, which splits), reconcile CHK-5's wording, and obtain the owner's recorded sign-off on the scoping — not a silent parenthetical.

title: The interpretation law is not total and not symmetric: outcomes the project has already produced fall into no branch
detail: Spec section 5's frozen interpretation law has three branches: (1) S3 > S0,S6 with S3 ~ S-PERM ~ S-ALT; (2) S3 > S-PERM stable -> anomaly, report and stop; (3) S3 ~ S0 -> report and stop. Missing branches include: S-PERM > S3 (by the equivariance argument this is EQUALLY impossible absent a bug, so the anomaly rule must be two-sided: |S3 - S-PERM| >= 0.02 stable in EITHER direction -> pipeline-integrity anomaly); S3 > S0 but S3 ~ S6 (typing content irrelevant, capacity/attention explains — the arc has already produced this: P1.2 recorded S3 - S6 = -0.0047 with S6 nominally highest, and the first pilot had S6 > S3); S6 or S7-class controls significantly ABOVE S3; S3 < S0; S3 > S-PERM in 2/3 seeds but below 0.02. Repo governance ('Claim status must come from a deterministic program reading raw result, frozen threshold, controls, hard-gate results' — CLAUDE.md research-governance rule; and the JSON-envelope-totality precedent from gate1a.2r.2b) requires a TOTAL deterministic status function; run_pilot_v3.py's status() is total via an else-catch-all, but the PATH B spec freezes prose bullets with gaps and names no status-emitter program among its deliverables. Fix at v0.2: enumerate the outcome partition exhaustively, add the symmetric S-PERM rule with the bug-diagnosis reading, map every cell to exactly one of the five dev labels (the vocabulary already includes INCONCLUSIVE_DEV_SIGNAL as a natural catch-all), and list the status program alongside the seven CHK programs. Also carry forward P1.3's per-question-type no-collapse condition, which the PATH B win criteria silently dropped.

title: Executable-check gaps: G-order unchecked, CHK-3 proves sufficiency not necessity, CHK-4's 0.25 is ~2x chance with no gate on the full surface family, CHK-7's solver unspecified, 'matched-ensemble member' undefined
detail: Walking the seven-requirement table (spec section 2.4) against 'anything without an executable check': (1) G-order (section 2.2) has NO CHK at all — nothing verifies order-dependence is real; the natural deterministic check is counterfactual: for every QB-ORD question, swapping the discourse positions of the two relevant same-class clauses must change the frozen solver's answer. Absent, requirement 4's 'order ... decide[s]' has no order-specific executable evidence. (2) CHK-3 counts questions whose SOLVER trace uses >= 2 edges — that measures the solver's route, not necessity; a 2-edge trace can coexist with a 1-edge shortcut (e.g., when the final-hop object happens to be unique passage-wide). Strengthen to a per-question necessity check: no single edge determines the answer uniquely. (3) CHK-4's bound of 0.25 on the single-op matcher is roughly DOUBLE candidate-uniform chance (v1 val uniform accuracy 0.12284 per CANDIDATE_UNIFORM_BASELINES.json; PATH B candidate sets are 'variable size' likewise), with no recorded justification; and only that ONE heuristic is bounded — B0-SURF, the full registered surface-heuristic family, is 'expected well below 1.0' with NO threshold, so a PATH B where richer surface heuristics still score near ceiling would sail through all seven checks while gutting requirement 4's substance (v1's B0 was 0.668 and B1 was 1.000 — surface strength is a demonstrated risk). Freeze a B0-SURF ceiling or record why not. (4) CHK-7's B-KEY is 'a solver' with no frozen family, capacity, or training budget — a weak solver passes <= uniform+0.05 vacuously; the check's strength IS the solver's strength, so the solver spec (e.g., the strongest of a registered family, trained to convergence) must be frozen at v0.2. (5) CHK-6's escape phrase 'or matched-ensemble member' is defined nowhere in the spec — a dangling concept in the one certificate that carries requirement 6.

title: (f) MAX_IDEAS=6 vs K=6..9: the frozen P1.3 packing crashes on any passage with more than 6 clauses
detail: The spec (section 5) says all arms reuse 'the FROZEN P1.3 architecture ... with no modification', and section 2.2 sets K (clauses per passage) in 6..9. But C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/exec/arms.py line 21 freezes MAX_IDEAS = 6, and C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_dev_gpu_pilot_v1/run_pilot_v3.py imports that constant (line 58) and allocates every batch tensor at that size in pack_batches_v3 (lines 130-163): h = zeros(b, MAX_IDEAS, 896) at line 134, then h[j, :n] = f['h'] at line 148. extract_split (cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/exec/activation_extraction.py, lines 80-86) stacks one row per clause with NO truncation, so for K=7..9 the assignment writes an (n,896) tensor into a slice-clamped (6,896) view -> RuntimeError. Same crash at p[j, :n] (line 159). The e_loc loop's 'if i < MAX_IDEAS' guard (line 156) would otherwise silently DROP clause indices >= 6 (deleting evidence, not failing closed). Instrumentation also hard-clamps: alpha[j, min(gi, MAX_IDEAS-1)] (line 379) and routed_acc's min(idxs[k+j], MAX_IDEAS-1) (line 433) misattribute any gold clause at index >= 6 to clause 5. Consequence: 'no modification' is unsatisfiable as written. The minimal fix (MAX_IDEAS 6 -> 9) edits the FROZEN claim-bearing Gate 1A package that the pilot README says is deliberately untouched — so the spec must either (a) declare a receipted PATH-B-local override of the packing constants (copy, not edit, the frozen file), or (b) cap K at 6 (my finding below shows K=6 does satisfy all four G-constraints, so 6..6 is viable but loses diversity). Either way the spec must say which, and the BINDING smoke gates it re-freezes must state the new shapes.

title: (b) Per-family answer-uniqueness constraints are NOT stated (only QB-INT has one); QB-COMP is concretely ambiguous
detail: Spec section 2.3 states a uniqueness guarantee only for QB-INT ('generator guarantees a unique element'). For QB-COMP 'which idea came to the mind that was drawn to X?' uniqueness needs TWO unstated constraints: (i) exactly one mind m with ^2(m, X) — G-multi encourages multiple ^2 instances and nothing forbids two minds drawn to the same X (even v1's law, C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/CONSTRUCTION_GOLD_DATASET_SPEC.md, only restricts one ^2 PER MIND); and (ii) exactly one ^8(a, b, m) targeting that mind m — v1's '^8 unique per (mind, idea_a)' pair-law explicitly ALLOWS multiple ^8 into the same mind from different sources a, and G-multi can be satisfied by exactly such duplicates, in which case 'came to the mind' cannot pick b: the question never mentions the source a. The same gap hits QB-ORD (if two of M's ^2 clauses both FOLLOW M's ^3(X) clause, 'the one whose clause FOLLOWS' is not unique — the rule needs 'exactly one follows' or 'the first following') and QB-REL (the anchored mind must have exactly one ^2, which conflicts with G-order if the generator anchors the question on the same mind that carries the ordered same-class pair). None of this is impossible — per-ASKED-question uniqueness side-constraints, enforced by the generator and fail-closed re-verified by the independent parser the way v1's _derive_answer does (len(hits)==1 else None, C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/tools/independent_roundtrip_checker.py lines 75-88), resolve it — but the v0.2 freeze must state each family's uniqueness law explicitly, or the generator+solver contract is incomplete and ambiguous questions will be generated.

title: (c) CHK-4's single-op matcher is undefined on PATH B: the v1 matcher abstains under multiplicity and cannot parse v2 questions at all
detail: CHK-4 requires 'the v1-style single-op matcher' to score <= 0.25. The actual v1 matcher has two behaviors that make the check as written either vacuous or unimplementable. First, its question grammar (_Q, C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/tools/independent_roundtrip_checker.py lines 58-63) matches only the four v1 question surfaces ('which idea was {mind} drawn to?'), which name the mind DIRECTLY; every PATH B question names its anchor relationally ('the mind that recoiled from X'), so the literal v1 matcher parses nothing, returns None, scores 0.000, and CHK-4 passes vacuously — proving only that the question templates changed, not that op-identification is insufficient. Second, if upgraded to parse v2 surfaces, its derivation rule 'return the object of the unique class-c clause' (via _derive_answer's len(hits)==1 else None) is UNDEFINED exactly where G-multi holds — CHK-1 guarantees >= 2 final-hop-class objects in >= 95% of passages, so the matcher abstains almost everywhere and again scores near 0 vacuously. The 0.25 threshold only means something for a GUESSING matcher, and the spec never pins the tie-break: first-match, last-match, uniform-random over class-c objects, or recency give different scores (a last-match rule could score far ABOVE 0.25 on QB-ORD, whose answer is by construction a later same-class clause). The spec must define B-1OP as a registered FAMILY of matchers (at minimum: first / last / uniform-over-class-objects tie-breaks, with the anchor entity resolved by oracle so the test isolates op-identification) and apply the 0.25 gate to the BEST member, else CHK-4 is not a deterministic program.

title: QB-XOP has no executable answer function — it is a dataset property, not a question family
detail: Section 2.3 defines QB-XOP as 'the same answer entity is reachable via different operation routes in different passages; question wording does not reveal the route class mix'. That is a cross-passage distributional property (essentially what CHK-2 measures), not a per-passage question with a derivation rule. The frozen graph solver (B1-GRAPH, required to score 1.000) cannot compute an answer for a family whose answer function is undefined, and 'per-family balance frozen in the dataset manifest' cannot be frozen for it. v0.2 must either give QB-XOP a concrete surface template + derivation (e.g., a wording shared verbatim between a ^2-route passage and an ^8-route passage, with the route recorded in the trace), or delete it as a family and keep the property inside CHK-2.

title: (d) CHK-2 'final-hop class' needs definition, and the >=30% threshold is carried entirely by ideas under the ^2/^8 pair
detail: For QB-INT the answer is produced by TWO ^6 edges plus one ^2 selector — there is no single final-hop EDGE, but both answer-producing edges share class ^6, so 'final-hop class' IS well-defined if v0.2 defines it as the class-set of the edges whose object is the answer in the frozen solver's edge-usage trace (QB-INT contributes {^6}). That definition line is currently missing. The bigger structural fact: with disjoint vocabularies (minds/ideas/parts, section 2.1), parts can ONLY ever be answers via ^6 (never 2 classes), minds are never answers in any listed family, and NO family has final-hop ^3 (QB-REL and QB-ORD end in ^2, QB-COMP in ^8, QB-INT in ^6) — so the '>= 30% of distinct answer entities under >= 2 final-hop classes' requirement can only be satisfied by ideas that are both a ^2-answer and an ^8-answer somewhere in the split. That is arithmetically easy if PATH B reuses v1-sized bundles (8 ideas per bundle: over 1000 passages every idea will almost surely be both, making the check near-vacuous) and the QB-INT part-answers permanently dilute the denominator. v0.2 should (i) define final-hop class as above, (ii) state the bundle sizes (unstated for v2), and (iii) decide whether the 30% denominator excludes part-type entities — otherwise the executable check is much weaker than owner requirement 2 sounds.

title: (e)+(f) Power risk: zero-overlap transfer + multi-hop questions on a frozen single-hop router — the arc's twice-documented all-arms-near-floor failure mode is likely to recur
detail: Two compounding risks, neither gated by the spec. (1) Surface diversity: 32 verbs must be partitioned verb-disjoint AND form-disjoint across families A,B (train), C (val), D (protected) — the allocation is unstated; any split like 4/2/2 per class leaves val only ~2 verbs x ~4 forms per class, and CHK-5's zero overlap means validation is pure zero-shot both lexically and syntactically. The arc already measured cross-family transfer as the primary bottleneck on the EASY v1 task (run_diagnostics: in-distribution 0.278 vs cross-family 0.210; P1.2b train ~0.78 vs val ~0.37). (2) Architecture: the frozen P1.3 MixtureHead (run_pilot_v3.py lines 167-217) is a SINGLE soft-attention router over clauses + clause-local answer experts. Multi-hop families (QB-COMP, QB-REL, QB-INT) require selecting the final-hop clause via an intermediate entity that only appears in ANOTHER clause; the router conditions only on the question vector g and per-clause h_i/p_i — it has no mechanism to condition on retrieved intermediate content. The best a profile can do is class-level routing, and G-multi guarantees >= 2 same-class clauses precisely so class-routing alone cannot finish the job — that is the intended bijection break, but it also means S3's expected effect shrinks to a small class-routing gain, on a harder task, under harsher transfer. The probable outcome is every arm compressed toward candidate-uniform, making Q-B1/Q-B2 uninterpretable — the exact 'ABOVE_UNIFORM_LOW_COMPETENCE_READOUT' situation the arc hit twice. v0.2 should add a pre-registered minimum-competence gate (e.g., S0 must exceed candidate-uniform by a frozen margin at val for the arm comparison to be interpretable) and note that owner requirement 4 is enforced only against B-1OP (CHK-4): B0-SURF has NO ceiling gate, so if richer surface heuristics score high the bijection break bought little and nothing fails closed. Also: the smoke-gate battery reuses gold_clause_index (single-gold-clause concept, from run_diagnostics.py) — undefined for 2-edge derivations; must be redefined as the solver-trace final-hop clause.

title: Reused pilot plumbing beyond the head module also breaks: profile assembly fails closed on the retired 16-verb inventory
detail: Section 5's 'no modification' can only cover the MixtureHead module itself. run_pilot_v3.py line 63 imports assemble from run_pilot_v2, whose S7H path calls s7_taxonomy_label (C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/cjt_gate1a_static_neural_v1/exec/labels.py lines 41-54), which regex-matches the 16 REGISTERED v1 head verbs and raises TAXONOMY_LOOKUP_FAILURE when exactly one is not found. PATH B retires all 16 verbs from clause rendering (section 3), so every clause fails the lookup. The new arm set (S0/S3/S6/S-PERM/S-ALT) also differs from the pilot's (S0/S3/S6/S7H/S7D): S-PERM needs a new frozen class-permutation source and S-ALT a new 32-verb WordNet table. All of this is dev-tree code, not the frozen Gate 1A package, so it is legitimately rewritable — but the spec should scope the freeze precisely ('the head module and optimizer/schedule constants are frozen; assembly, packing dimensions, and profile sources are PATH-B-local') instead of the current blanket 'no modification', which is false on its face.
